mainTopic: Which blemishes allow a בכור to be slaughtered: why the blemish must be visible and permanent, and the exact measures for ear blemishes (split, notch, hole, dried-out ear)
overview: The גמרא first explains why a בכור may be slaughtered only for a blemish that is both visible and permanent. 'מום רע' rules out a hidden blemish. A temporary blemish is ruled out by a קל וחומר from פדיון, which a ברייתא on ויקרא 27 supports, or else by the words 'lame and blind.' Next it goes through the ear blemishes in the משנה. A split counts at any size, a notch counts if a fingernail catches in it, and a dried-out ear is defined in two ways. For the size of a hole, the ת״ק says a כרשינה and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says a lentil, and the גמרא notes that these two are nearly the same. A contradiction from piercing a slave's ear is answered: a lentil-size hole is needed to permit slaughter, but a tiny hole already disqualifies the animal from the מזבח. The גמרא then asks whether a 'full כרשינה' means a hole the bean passes through. רב הונא רבה answers from a similar case, the משנה about a damaged skull. This leads to a side discussion about whether בית הלל's measure is a סלע, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Why only extracted gums and not damaged ones?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notices that the rule about the inner gums counts only when they are pulled out, and asks why damage or scratches do not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the inner gums were pulled out, yes, it is a blemish. If they were only chipped or scratched, is it not a blemish?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the earlier ruling about the inner gums closely and asks why only full extraction counts. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Pulling the gums out is a blemish that allows a בכור to be slaughtered. The wording suggests that mere damage or scratching does not count. The גמרא wants to know what makes the difference.

phrases.english: If they were pulled out, yes (it counts as a blemish),
phrases.notes: This is about the animal's inner gums, which were just discussed.

phrases.english: but if they were damaged or scratched, no?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why damage to the inner gums does not count as a blemish when extraction does.

steps.title: A hidden blemish is not a 'מום רע'
steps.stepSummary: The answer is that the תורה requires a 'מום רע', and a hidden blemish does not qualify.
steps.simpleTranslation: I need a 'bad blemish', and this is not one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that damage inside the mouth is hidden, so it is not the 'מום רע' the תורה requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מום רע' mean a blemish that is visible and degrading. Fully pulled-out gums meet that standard. Chipped or scratched gums stay hidden inside the mouth, so they do not.

keyTerms.meaning: a 'bad' blemish, meaning visible and degrading

phrases.english: I require an 'ill blemish,' and there is none!

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תורה requires a 'מום רע', a visible blemish, and a hidden blemish is not one.

steps.title: Then a temporary blemish should also count
steps.stepSummary: If every visible blemish counts, then a מום עובר should count too. So why does the משנה say a tear in the skin of the ear does not allow slaughter?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, a temporary blemish should also count! Why then did we learn: 'but not from the skin'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the only test is visibility, then a visible temporary blemish should also allow slaughter.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'מום רע' seemed to exclude only hidden blemishes. A tear in the skin of the ear is visible but will heal. The משנה still does not count it, so something besides 'מום רע' must be excluding it.

keyTerms.meaning: a temporary blemish that will heal
why then did we learn (in the משנה)

phrases.english: If so, a temporary blemish too (should count)!
Why did we learn: 'but not from the skin'?

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that 'מום רע' excludes only hidden blemishes
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A visible temporary blemish passes the 'מום רע' test, yet the משנה does not count it.

steps.title: Temporary blemish is excluded by סברא
steps.stepSummary: The מום עובר is excluded by logic, not by the פסוק. We do not redeem קדשים because of it, so we certainly do not slaughter a בכור because of it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A temporary blemish is excluded by logic. Now, if we do not redeem an animal because of it, would we slaughter (a בכור) because of it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the rule about a מום עובר comes from a קל וחומר based on פדיון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Redeeming קדשים is a milder step than slaughtering a בכור outside the מקדש. If a מום עובר does not even allow redemption, it surely does not allow slaughter. So 'מום רע' only needs to exclude hidden blemishes.

phrases.english: A temporary blemish is (excluded by) logic:
now, we do not even redeem because of it;
would we slaughter (a בכור) because of it?

steps.terutzResolutionType: Different source: logic rather than the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'מום רע' must exclude every non-qualifying blemish, so a visible temporary one should qualify.
steps.terutzMaskana: A מום עובר is excluded by a קל וחומר from פדיון, and 'מום רע' only excludes hidden blemishes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This explains why a בכור needs a blemish that is both visible and permanent, and where each requirement comes from.

steps.title: ברייתא: the פסוק speaks of blemished animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that קדשים are not redeemed because of a מום עובר. It opens by reading 'בהמה טמאה' in ויקרא 27:11 as blemished animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'And if it be any impure animal, of which they may not bring an offering to ה'.' The verse is speaking of blemished animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a ברייתא to support the claim from step 4 that we do not redeem because of a מום עובר. This line sets up the reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that the 'impure animal' in this פסוק is really a kosher animal with a blemish, which cannot be offered. The next lines defend this reading and then use it for the מום עובר rule.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is taught (in a ברייתא)

phrases.english: As it is taught: 'And if it be any impure animal,'

phrases.aramaic: אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קׇרְבָּן לַה׳״ —
phrases.english: 'of which they may not bring an offering to the Lord' —
the verse is speaking of blemished animals.

steps.raayaObject: That קדשים are not redeemed because of a מום עובר

steps.title: Maybe it means a truly non-kosher animal?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the פסוק might simply mean a real non-kosher animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you say the verse speaks of blemished animals that were redeemed, or does it speak only of an actual impure animal?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא questions its own reading by suggesting the simple meaning, an actual non-kosher animal. This sets up its proof in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read simply, 'בהמה טמאה' means an animal like a donkey. If that were the meaning, the פסוק would teach nothing about redeeming a blemished kosher animal.

phrases.aramaic: אַתָּה אוֹמֵר בְּבַעֲלֵי מוּמִין שֶׁנִּפְדּוּ הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר,
phrases.english: Do you say the verse speaks of blemished animals that were redeemed,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא בִּבְהֵמָה טְמֵאָה מַמָּשׁ?
phrases.english: or is it only about an actual impure animal?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether 'בהמה טמאה' in ויקרא 27:11 means a blemished kosher animal or a literally non-kosher one.

steps.title: Another פסוק already covers non-kosher animals
steps.stepSummary: Since ויקרא 27:27 already speaks of a real non-kosher animal, ויקרא 27:11 must mean blemished animals that are redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: When it says 'And if it be of the impure animal', an impure animal is already mentioned. So how do I explain 'of which they may not bring'? You must say: this is blemished animals that were redeemed.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא proves its reading: a later פסוק already covers real non-kosher animals, so this פסוק must be about something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה does not repeat itself for no reason. Since a real non-kosher animal is covered in 27:27, 27:11 teaches that blemished kosher קדשים can be redeemed.

phrases.english: When it says 'And if it be of the impure animal,'
an impure animal is already mentioned;

phrases.aramaic: הָא מָה אֲנִי מְקַיֵּים ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה״?
phrases.english: so how do I explain 'of which they may not bring'?

phrases.aramaic: הֱוֵי אוֹמֵר: זֶה בַּעֲלֵי מוּמִין שֶׁנִּפְדּוּ.
phrases.english: You must say: this is blemished animals that were redeemed.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Real non-kosher animals are covered by 27:27, so 27:11 teaches the redemption of blemished kosher קדשים.

steps.title: No redemption for a temporary blemish
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא concludes that only an animal that can never be offered may be redeemed. One with a מום עובר could be offered later, so it may not be redeemed.
steps.simpleTranslation: One might think they may be redeemed because of a temporary blemish. The verse says 'of which they may not bring an offering to ה'': an animal that is never offered at all. This excludes one that cannot be offered today but can be tomorrow.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives the key point the גמרא needed: a מום עובר does not allow פדיון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אשר לא יקריבו' describes an animal that can never be offered. A temporary blemish will heal, so the animal can still be offered later. This completes the proof for the סברא in step 4: no redemption for a מום עובר, and so certainly no slaughter of a בכור.
steps.whatToRemember: A בכור may be slaughtered only for a blemish that is visible (from 'מום רע') and permanent (by קל וחומר from פדיון). קדשים are redeemed only when they can never be offered, so a מום עובר is not enough.

phrases.english: One might think they may be redeemed because of a temporary blemish?

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר לֹא יַקְרִיבוּ מִמֶּנָּה קׇרְבָּן לַה׳״ —
phrases.english: The verse says: 'of which they may not bring an offering to the Lord' —
one that is not offered at all;
this excludes one that is not offered today
but can be offered tomorrow.

steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: קדשים with a מום עובר are not redeemed, which confirms the סברא that a בכור is not slaughtered because of a מום עובר.

steps.title: Second answer: lame and blind teach that only permanent blemishes count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא offers another reason why a מום עובר is not included in 'כל מום רע'. If every blemish counted, the פסוק would not need to name 'lame' and 'blind'. Naming them shows that only permanent blemishes like them count.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you want, say this instead: if even a temporary blemish counted, why would the פסוק need to say 'lame' and 'blind'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, separate answer to why a מום עובר does not let us slaughter a בכור. This time the answer comes from the wording of the פסוק itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 used logic: if we don't redeem קדשים for a מום עובר, we surely don't slaughter a בכור for one. Here the answer comes from the פסוק: 'lame' and 'blind' are permanent blemishes, so they teach that 'any bad blemish' means only permanent ones like them.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say: this opens a second, alternative answer
If so: if your idea were true
Lame and blind, the two blemishes named in the פסוק
Why do I need it? Used to show that a word in the פסוק must be teaching something

steps.whatToRemember: There are two reasons a מום עובר does not permit slaughtering a בכור: logic from קדשים (step 4), and the wording 'lame and blind', which shows that only permanent blemishes count.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the basic rule for all the blemishes that follow: only a lasting blemish lets a בכור be slaughtered outside the Temple.

phrases.english: If you wish, say:

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן פִּסֵּחַ וְעִוֵּר לְמָה לִי?
phrases.english: If so, why do I need 'lame' and 'blind'?
phrases.notes: דברים 15:21. The פסוק says 'lame or blind, any bad blemish'; 'if so' means if a temporary blemish counted too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer, alongside the logical answer of step 4 that the ברייתא in steps 5-8 backed up.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק closely: the specific examples limit the general phrase
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Any bad blemish' might include even a temporary one.
steps.terutzMaskana: Naming 'lame' and 'blind', which are permanent, shows that only permanent blemishes count.

steps.title: A split ear: any size counts, and a notch counts whatever caused it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about a split ear and brings a ברייתא. A split of any size is a blemish. A notch counts whether a person or heaven caused it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: the ear was split, even though nothing is missing. The Rabbis taught: a split counts at any size. A notch counts whether a person caused it or it happened naturally.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה, about a split ear, and quotes a ברייתא that explains it. This sets up a question about the ברייתא's wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A split (סדק) is a crack where no part of the ear is missing. The ברייתא says even a tiny one counts. For a notch (פגימה), it adds that the cause does not matter. The wording mentions the cause only for the notch, and the next step picks up on that.

keyTerms.meaning: A split or crack, where nothing is missing
A notch or nick, where a piece is missing
Any amount at all, even the smallest
By heaven: happening naturally, not caused by a person

phrases.aramaic: נִסְדְּקָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא חָסְרָה.
phrases.english: It was split, even though it is not lacking.
phrases.notes: This quotes our משנה about the ear of a בכור.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
The split: any size at all;

phrases.aramaic: הַפְּגִימָה — בֵּין בִּידֵי אָדָם בֵּין בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם.
phrases.english: the notch: whether by the hand of a person or by the hand of heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִסְדְּקָה אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא חָסְרָה. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next ear blemish in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A split of any size is a blemish, and a notch is a blemish whether a person or heaven caused it.

steps.title: Does a naturally caused split not count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's wording. Since it says 'by person or heaven' only about the notch, does that mean a split caused naturally does not count?
steps.simpleTranslation: Does that mean that a split caused by heaven does not count?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads the ברייתא closely and finds a troubling implication in how it is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא spelled out 'person or heaven' only for the notch. That seems to suggest a split counts only when a person caused it. That makes no sense, because a natural split is just as much a blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: This implies that: drawing a conclusion from how something is worded

phrases.english: Does this imply that a split
caused by heaven does not count?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא in step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's wording, which gives 'person or heaven' only for the notch
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Because the cause is mentioned only for the notch, it sounds as if a natural split does not count, which cannot be right.

steps.title: Correct reading: both a split and a notch count, whatever the cause
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא so that 'whether by heaven or by a person' applies to both the split and the notch.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it this way: a split and a notch both count, whether heaven or a person caused them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the ברייתא differently, so the phrase about the cause covers both blemishes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the cause does not matter for either the split or the notch. This removes the strange idea that a natural split would not count.

keyTerms.meaning: By a person: caused by a human

phrases.english: Rather,
a split and a notch:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם בֵּין בִּידֵי אָדָם.
phrases.english: whether by the hand of heaven or by the hand of a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 11.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only a notch counts from either cause, so a natural split would not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both a split and a notch count, whether heaven or a person caused them.

steps.title: How big must a notch be?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks what the minimum size of a notch is.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how big does a notch have to be?
steps.whatsHappening: Since a split counts at any size, the ברייתא now asks how big a notch must be. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A split needs no minimum size. A notch is treated differently, so a measure is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: A set amount or minimum size

phrases.english: And how much is the measure of a notch?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא and moves from which notches count to how big they must be.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum size of a notch that counts as a blemish

steps.title: A notch must be big enough to catch a fingernail
steps.stepSummary: A notch counts if it is big enough that a fingernail catches in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Big enough that a fingernail catches in it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers with a simple hands-on test: run a fingernail along the ear and see if it catches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The measure is practical. If the gap is deep enough to hold back a fingernail, it is a real notch and counts as a blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: That it catches or holds back

steps.whatToRemember: A split counts at any size. A notch counts if a fingernail catches in it. For both, the cause does not matter.

phrases.english: Enough that a fingernail catches in it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A notch counts once it is deep enough for a fingernail to catch in it.

steps.title: Size of a hole in the ear: a vetch or a lentil
steps.stepSummary: Quoting the משנה about a pierced ear, a ברייתא sets the hole's size. The ת״ק says the size of a כרשינה (vetch). רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says the size of a lentil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: it was pierced with a hole the full size of... The Rabbis taught: how big is a hole in the ear? The size of a vetch. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: like a lentil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next blemish in the משנה, a hole in the ear, and brings a ברייתא with two opinions about its size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion sets the size at a כרשינה, a small bean. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה sets it at a lentil. These are two different measures for the same blemish.

keyTerms.meaning: It was pierced, with a hole
A vetch, a small bean used as a measure
A תנא who argues with the first opinion here

phrases.english: It was pierced, the full size of, etc.
The Rabbis taught: how big is the piercing of the ear?
The full size of a vetch.
Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda says:
Like a lentil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the next ear blemish in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A hole in the ear counts if it is the size of a vetch; רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says the size of a lentil.

steps.title: What counts as a dried-out ear
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא defines a dried-out ear: if pierced, it gives no drop of blood. רבי יוסי בן המשולם says it must be so dry that it crumbles.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is a dried-out ear? One that, if pierced, does not give out a drop of blood. רבי יוסי בן המשולם says: dried out means so dry that it crumbles.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to another ear blemish from the משנה, a dried-out ear, and gives two definitions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first opinion uses a test: prick the ear, and if no blood comes out, it is dried out. רבי יוסי בן המשולם requires more: the ear must be so dry that it crumbles. His standard is stricter.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא with a stricter definition of a dried-out ear

steps.whatToRemember: Ear blemishes have set measures: a split of any size, a notch that catches a fingernail, a hole the size of a vetch (or a lentil), and a dried-out ear (no blood when pricked, or so dry it crumbles).

phrases.english: And what is a dried-out ear?
One that, if it is pierced,
does not give out a drop of blood.
Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam says:
Dried out means so dry that it crumbles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and moves to the next ear blemish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A dried-out ear is one that gives no blood when pricked; רבי יוסי בן המשולם requires that it be dry enough to crumble.

steps.title: A teaching: their words are almost the same
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that the two opinions just quoted are close to being identical.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: Their words are close to being the same.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a short ברייתא saying that two opinions are nearly the same in practice. This sets up the next question: which two opinions does it mean?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 15 and 16 gave two separate disagreements: one about the size of the hole and one about a dried-out ear. This line does not say which pair it refers to, so the גמרא has to work that out.

phrases.english: It was taught:
Their words are close to being the same.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a comment on the disagreements quoted in steps 15 and 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two of the opinions quoted are practically almost the same.

steps.title: Whose words are almost the same?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which two opinions the ברייתא is calling nearly identical.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose words are these?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple clarifying question: which two תנאים is the ברייתא talking about?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible pairs of opinions, from step 15 and step 16. The גמרא needs to choose one.

phrases.english: Their words, of whom?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks who is meant in the ברייתא of step 17.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which pair of disputing opinions the ברייתא calls nearly the same.

steps.title: Not the two views on a dried-out ear
steps.stepSummary: It cannot mean the ת״ק and רבי יוסי בן המשולם, because their views are very different.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means the ת״ק and רבי יוסי בן המשולם, there is a big difference between them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the dried-out-ear pair and immediately rejects it, because those two opinions are far apart.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One opinion says an ear counts as dried out when no blood comes out. The other says it must be so dry that it crumbles. That is a large gap, so they cannot be called 'close to the same.'

keyTerms.meaning: if you say (a suggestion about to be rejected)

phrases.english: If you say: of the first תנא
and Rabbi Yosei ben HaMeshullam,
phrases.notes: These are the two views on a dried-out ear from step 16: no drop of blood, against crumbling.

phrases.english: there is a lot (of difference)!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵימָא דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן הַמְשׁוּלָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one possible answer to step 18 and rejects it.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects identifying the pair as the two views on a dried-out ear.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Those opinions are far apart, not 'nearly the same.'

steps.title: It means the two views on the size of the hole
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא means the ת״ק (a כרשינה) and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה (a lentil), which are almost the same size.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means the ת״ק and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its answer: the 'nearly the same' opinions are the two sizes for the hole in a pierced ear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כרשינה and a lentil are very close in size. So the ברייתא is saying that this disagreement makes almost no difference in practice.
steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's 'nearly the same' refers to כרשינה against lentil, the size of the hole in a pierced ear.

phrases.english: Rather, of the first תנא
and Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.
phrases.notes: These are the two views from step 15: a כרשינה against a lentil.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct answer after rejecting the first suggestion.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The pair is the ת״ק and רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה on the size of the hole.

steps.title: Must the hole be as big as a lentil? A contradiction from piercing a slave's ear
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's lentil size. It brings a ברייתא that includes small tools, like a needle, for piercing a slave's ear.
steps.simpleTranslation: The size of a lentil, yes; less than a lentil, no? But there is a contradiction: 'An awl.' I only know an awl. From where do we include a palm thorn, a thorn, a needle, a drill and a writing stylus?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a challenge against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. It begins quoting a ברייתא about which tools may be used to pierce the ear of an עבד עברי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said a pierced ear counts only if the hole is as big as a lentil. The ברייתא includes thin tools like a needle, which make a much smaller hole. The full force of the contradiction builds over the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: and they contrasted it (introduces a contradicting source)

phrases.english: The size of a lentil, yes;
less than a lentil, no?
But raise a contradiction:
'An awl': I have only an awl.
From where do we include the palm thorn, and the thorn,
and the needle, and the drill, and the stylus?

steps.triggerLanguage: כַּעֲדָשָׁה — אִין, בְּצִיר מִכַּעֲדָשָׁה — לָא? וּרְמִינְהִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from identifying the opinions to challenging רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's size.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's rule that the hole must be the size of a lentil.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the law of piercing a slave's ear, small tools like a needle are included, and they make a hole smaller than a lentil.

steps.title: Anything held in the hand, or only metal
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה learns from 'and you shall take' that any hand-held tool is valid. רבי allows only metal tools.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'and you shall take': anything taken by hand. These are the words of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. רבי says: 'Awl': just as an awl is special in being metal, so too anything made of metal.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא. It shows that the opinion including a needle belongs to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the key point for the challenge. The same תנא who requires a lentil-sized hole also allows a needle, which makes a tiny hole. רבי disagrees and limits the tools to metal ones, like an awl.
steps.confusionAlert: Here 'רבי' with no name is רבי יהודה הנשיא, not רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. It is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה who allows a needle.

phrases.english: The verse says: 'And you shall take':
anything that is taken by hand,
the words of Rabbi Yosei son of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi says: 'An awl':
just as an awl is special in being made of metal,
so too anything made of metal.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״וְלָקַחְתָּ״ — כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁנִּלְקָח בַּיָּד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the first part of the contradicting ברייתא and names who holds which view.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה: any hand-held tool may be used to pierce. רבי: only metal tools.

steps.title: The end of the ברייתא: pierce only in the earlobe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the end of the ברייתא: they pierce the slave's ear only in the earlobe. This adds the last piece of the challenge.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the end of the ברייתא teaches: רבי said: יודן בריבי would teach: When they pierce, they pierce only in the earlobe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds the closing line of the same ברייתא, about where on the ear the piercing is done. It is collecting this piece for the challenge, which it spells out in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יודן בריבי's view is that the piercing is done in the soft earlobe, and a hole there would not be a blemish. The חכמים reject this in the next step, and their view, that the piercing is in the upper ear, is what drives the challenge against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.

keyTerms.meaning: and the end (of the source) teaches

phrases.english: And the end teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי, יוּדָן בְּרִבִּי הָיָה דּוֹרֵשׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi said: Yudan the distinguished would teach:
phrases.notes: Some versions say רבי אלעזר here instead of just 'רבי.' 'בריבי' is a title of honor, like 'the distinguished one.'

phrases.english: When they pierce,
they pierce only in the earlobe.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא: אָמַר רַבִּי, יוּדָן בְּרִבִּי הָיָה דּוֹרֵשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the סיפא of the same ברייתא to finish building the contradiction.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's lentil-sized hole for a pierced ear.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: This line gives the earlobe view, which the חכמים reject in the next line. Their position, that piercing is in the upper ear and blemishes a כהן, combined with רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה allowing a needle, shows that a hole smaller than a lentil is a מום.

steps.title: The Sages say a pierced kohen slave becomes blemished
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא ends with the חכמים: a כהן who is an עבד עברי is not pierced, because piercing makes him a בעל מום. That only works if the piercing is in the upper ear, so even a needle-size hole counts as a מום.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages say: a Hebrew slave who is a כהן is not pierced, because it would make him blemished. If the piercing were in the earlobe, how could it blemish him? So piercing must be done on the upper part of the ear.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the ברייתא. This last line completes the challenge against רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים say piercing turns a כהן into a בעל מום. An earlobe hole would not do that, so the piercing must be in the upper ear. That means even a small hole, like one from a needle, counts as a מום. So how can רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה require a hole the size of a lentil?

keyTerms.meaning: Someone or something with a blemish, which disqualifies a כהן from Temple service or an animal from the מזבח
Has his ear pierced (the עבד עברי who chooses to stay with his master)
The upper, harder part of the ear

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two places on the ear. A hole in the soft earlobe is not a blemish. A hole in the upper ear is, and the חכמים are talking about the upper ear.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
A Hebrew slave who is a כהן is not pierced,
because he becomes blemished.
phrases.notes: A blemished כהן cannot serve in the Temple, so we don't pierce him.

phrases.english: And if you say they would pierce in the earlobe,

phrases.aramaic: הֵיאַךְ עֶבֶד כֹּהֵן נַעֲשֶׂה בַּעַל מוּם?
phrases.english: how does a slave who is a כהן become blemished?

phrases.aramaic: הָא אֵין רוֹצְעִין אֶלָּא בְּגוֹבַהּ שֶׁל אוֹזֶן.
phrases.english: This shows they pierce only on the upper part of the ear.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֵין עֶבֶד עִבְרִי כֹּהֵן נִרְצָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא quoted in steps 21-23 and adds the last piece of the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's rule that the hole must be the size of a lentil
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He allows a needle for piercing, and the חכמים say piercing the upper ear blemishes a כהן. So a needle-size hole, smaller than a lentil, is already a מום.

steps.title: Two different sizes: one for slaughtering, one for disqualifying
steps.stepSummary: רב חנא בר קטינא answers that a lentil-size hole is needed to allow slaughtering the בכור, while even a tiny hole is enough to disqualify it from the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר קטינא said: It is not difficult. Here it is about slaughtering, there it is about disqualifying.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנא בר קטינא answers the challenge by showing there are two different rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A tiny hole is enough to make the animal unfit for the מזבח, just as a needle hole blemishes a כהן. But to permit slaughtering the בכור as a blemished animal, the hole must reach the size of a lentil. So רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's lentil measure and the needle case do not contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This opens an answer that shows two sources are about different cases
To slaughter. Here it means permitting the blemished בכור to be slaughtered and eaten
To disqualify, meaning to make it unfit for the מזבח

steps.whatToRemember: There are two levels of ear holes. A tiny hole makes the animal unfit for the מזבח. A lentil-size hole is needed before the בכור may be slaughtered.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that one blemish can have different size limits, depending on which rule we are asking about.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥana bar Ketina said:
It is not difficult: here it is about slaughtering,
phrases.notes: "Here" is רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's lentil size: that much is needed to allow the בכור to be slaughtered.

phrases.english: there it is about disqualifying.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא — כָּאן לִשְׁחוֹט, כָּאן לִפְסוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge built in steps 21-24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splits the cases (כאן ... כאן): two different rules with two different sizes
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought one size decides every rule about a blemish, so the needle hole contradicts the lentil size.
steps.terutzMaskana: Lentil size is for permitting slaughter. A smaller hole is enough to disqualify from the מזבח.

steps.title: What is a כרשינה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what a כרשינה is, and רב שרביא says it is called הינדא.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a כרשינה? רב שרביא said: הינדא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the ת״ק's measure, the כרשינה, and asks what that word means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ת״ק measured the hole by a כרשינה, so we need to know what plant that is. רב שרביא gives its Aramaic name, הינדא, which is a kind of vetch seed.

keyTerms.meaning: What is? It asks for the meaning of a word
A vetch seed, a small bean used as a size measure
The Aramaic name for the כרשינה

phrases.english: What is a karshina?
Rav Sherevya said: hinda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the lentil discussion and defines the ת״ק's measure.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which plant the word כרשינה refers to
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב שרביא: it is the הינדא (a vetch seed).

steps.title: Must the bean pass through the hole or just fit in it?
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא asks רב הונא רבה whether the measure means a hole a כרשינה can go in and out of, or a hole the כרשינה just fills.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא asked רב הונא רבה: Does it mean a כרשינה that goes in and out, or a כרשינה that stays in place?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know what a כרשינה is, רב הושעיא asks how exactly to use it as a measure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the bean must go in and out easily, the hole has to be a bit bigger than the bean. If the bean only needs to sit snugly, the hole is exactly the bean's size. The question is which of these the measure means.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him. One scholar asks another a question
That goes in and comes out, meaning it passes through freely
That stands, meaning it sits fixed in the hole

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא מֵרַב הוּנָא רַבָּה:
phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya asked Rav Huna the Great:
Is it a karshina that goes in and comes out,
or a karshina that stays in place?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא מֵרַב הוּנָא רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the definition of כרשינה by asking how the measure works.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the hole must let the bean pass through, so it is slightly bigger, or only hold it, so it is exactly the bean's size

steps.title: I didn't hear this, but I heard something similar
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא רבה says he never heard a ruling on this exact question, but he did hear a ruling on a similar case.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: This I did not hear. Something like it I did hear.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא רבה starts his answer. He admits he has no direct tradition on this case and points to a similar one. This sets up the next part of the discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He does not answer straight from a ruling about this case. He plans to learn the answer from a parallel case he did hear about.

keyTerms.meaning: This I did not hear. He has no tradition on this exact case
Something like it I did hear. He will compare it to a similar case

phrases.english: He said to him: This I did not hear,
something like it I did hear.

steps.triggerLanguage: זוֹ לֹא שָׁמַעְתִּי, כַּיּוֹצֵא בָּהּ שָׁמַעְתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to רב הושעיא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No direct tradition on this case. He will answer by comparing it to a similar case he did hear about.

steps.title: The similar case: a spine or skull with a piece missing
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא רבה quotes a משנה. A spine or skull with a piece missing does not make טומאה in a tent. בית שמאי and בית הלל argue about how much must be missing.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: a spine and a skull that are missing a piece do not make טומאה in a tent. How much must be missing from the spine? בית שמאי say two vertebrae, and בית הלל say one vertebra. For the skull, בית שמאי say a piece the size of a drilled hole, and בית הלל say enough that if it were taken from a living person, he would die.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא רבה now tells us the similar case he heard about. It is a משנה about how big a missing piece of spine or skull must be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A whole spine or skull of a dead person makes טומאה in a tent, but a damaged one does not. The argument is about how much damage counts. For the skull, בית שמאי give a fixed size (a drilled hole), while בית הלל give a size based on what would kill a living person. That second measure is unclear, and the next steps try to pin it down.

keyTerms.meaning: makes טומאה pass to everything under the same roof
one vertebra (one bone of the spine)
a drill; here, the size of a drilled hole

steps.confusionAlert: Here בית הלל are more lenient than בית שמאי. A smaller missing piece is enough for them to say the spine no longer makes טומאה.

phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: the spine and the skull that are missing a piece,
how much must be missing from the spine
so that it will not make טומאה in a tent?
בית שמאי say: two vertebrae,
and בית הלל say: one vertebra.

phrases.aramaic: וּבַגּוּלְגּוֹלֶת, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: כִּמְלֹא מַקְדֵּחַ,
phrases.english: And for the skull, בית שמאי say: the size of a drilled hole,
and בית הלל say: an amount that, if it were taken
from a living person, he would die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the content of the similar case רב הונא רבה said he heard about.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For the skull, בית שמאי require a missing piece the size of a drilled hole. בית הלל require a missing piece big enough to kill a living person.

steps.title: רב חסדא asks how big the measure of בית הלל is
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא asks what size בית הלל mean by 'enough that a living person would die.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חסדא was sitting and asked: 'Enough that if it were taken from a living person he would die.' How much is that?
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא asks for an actual size behind בית הלל's measure for the skull.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל's measure describes a result (the person would die), not a size you can check. רב חסדא wants a number that can actually be measured.

keyTerms.meaning: he had a question, he was unsure

phrases.english: And רב חסדא was sitting and asked:
'An amount that if taken from a living person' — how much is that?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the exact size of בית הלל's measure in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The actual size of 'enough to kill a living person' for a hole in the skull.

steps.title: The answer: the size of a סלע coin
steps.stepSummary: רב תחליפא בר אבודימי quotes שמואל: the measure is the size of a סלע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב תחליפא בר אבודימי said to him: This is what שמואל said: it is the size of a סלע.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא gets an answer. בית הלל's measure is a hole the size of a סלע coin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now there is a clear size you can measure: a סלע coin. This exchange between רב חסדא and רב תחליפא is a side discussion about בית הלל's measure for the skull. The similar case רב הונא רבה cited is the משנה in step 29, which uses the wording 'מלא מקדח'. How this whole discussion answers his question becomes clear only on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: a large silver coin, used here as a size

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי:
phrases.english: רב תחליפא בר אבודימי said to him:
This is what שמואל said: the size of a סלע.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב תַּחְלִיפָא בַּר אֲבוּדִימִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב חסדא's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The hole must be the size of a סלע coin.

steps.title: Did the answer come from שמואל or from a ברייתא?
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא says רב תחליפא quoted a teaching of an אמורא. רב שמואל בר יהודה says he quoted a ברייתא. The גמרא gives a memory aid.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: רב ספרא said he told him a teaching of an אמורא, and רב שמואל בר יהודה said he told him a ברייתא. Your memory aid: 'רב שמואל בר יהודה teaches (תני).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to record a side argument. People disagreed about the source of רב תחליפא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides agree the answer was 'a סלע'. They only argue about whether it came from שמואל, an אמורא, or from a ברייתא of the תנאים. The word תני ('teaches') usually goes with a ברייתא, so it helps you remember that רב שמואל בר יהודה is the one who said ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: a teaching of the תנאים (here, a ברייתא)
and it was stated (a report of an argument)

phrases.english: And it was stated: רב ספרא said:
He told him a teaching of an אמורא,
and רב שמואל בר יהודה said:
He told him a ברייתא.

phrases.aramaic: וְסִימָנָיךְ: תָּנֵי רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר יְהוּדָה.
phrases.english: And your memory aid: 'רב שמואל בר יהודה teaches.'
phrases.notes: 'Teaches' (תני) is the word usually used for a ברייתא, so the one with this phrase is the one who said 'ברייתא.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side note about where the answer 'a סלע' came from.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides agree on the measure, a סלע. They argue only about whether its source was שמואל or a ברייתא.

steps.title: רב חסדא: then בית שמאי and בית הלל would be saying the same thing
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא objects that if בית הלל mean a סלע, their opinion is the same as בית שמאי's.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he said to him: If so, you have made the words of בית שמאי and the words of בית הלל one and the same!
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא pushes back on the answer 'a סלע.' He says it would wipe out the argument between בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי's measure is a drilled hole. רב חסדא holds that a drilled hole is the same size as a סלע. If so, בית הלל saying 'a סלע' would match בית שמאי exactly, and there would be nothing to argue about.

phrases.english: And he said to him: If so,
phrases.notes: רב חסדא is speaking to רב תחליפא.

and the words of בית הלל one and the same!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִם כֵּן, עָשִׂיתָה דִּבְרֵי בֵּית שַׁמַּאי וְדִבְרֵי בֵּית הִלֵּל אֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that בית הלל's measure is a סלע.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A drilled hole (בית שמאי's measure) is the size of a סלע. So the answer would make the two opinions the same, which cannot be right for two sides that are arguing.

steps.title: A משנה about window sizes, quoted to prove the point
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא starts quoting a משנה about the size of a window not made by people. It is a large fist, the fist of בן אבטיח, which רבי יוסי says is like a large human head.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: a window that was not made by people, its size is a full large fist, and this is the fist of בן אבטיח. רבי יוסי said: and it is like a large human head.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא begins bringing a source to show that a drilled hole equals a סלע. This line is the start of the quote. The part that actually mentions the drill comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists sizes of openings that let טומאה pass from room to room. The first size is for a window that formed by itself: a large fist. The quote continues past this point, and the part about the drilled hole and the סלע is what will prove רב חסדא's claim.

keyTerms.meaning: a window, an opening for light
a man known for his very large fist

phrases.aramaic: דִּתְנַן: מָאוֹר שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשָׂה בִּידֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: As we learned in a משנה: a window that was not made by human hands,
its size is a full large fist,
and this is the fist of בן אבטיח.
רבי יוסי said:
And it is like the size of a large human head.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּתְנַן: מָאוֹר שֶׁלֹּא נַעֲשָׂה בִּידֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts bringing the source behind רב חסדא's claim that a drilled hole equals a סלע.
steps.raayaObject: That a drilled hole and a סלע are the same size, so the two opinions would match.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in כלים listing the sizes of openings, which continues past this point.

steps.title: A window made by people is measured by the size of a סלע
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה continues: a window made by people only needs to be the size of the hole of the large Temple drill. That equals an Italian פונדיון or a סלע of Nero.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if the window was made by people, its measure is the full size of the hole of the large drill of the chamber, which is like an Italian פונדיון and like a סלע of Nero. And its size is...
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא is still in the middle of quoting the משנה he began in step 34. He is not done yet, so this step sets up the point he will make once the quote is finished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה contrasts two kinds of windows. A natural opening needs to be as big as a large fist, but a man-made one only needs to be the size of a drill hole, which equals a סלע coin. This brings the סלע measure into the discussion, the same measure שמואל gave for בית הלל in step 31.

steps.whyThisMatters: The משנה connects the man-made window measure to the size of a סלע, the same measure שמואל gave. רב חסדא will use this when he finishes quoting the source.
